# SST Laravel — agent quick reference

Deploy Laravel on AWS Fargate (containers). Full docs:
`node_modules/@kirschbaum-development/sst-laravel/docs/` (guides listed in
`README.md`, every option in `api.md`).

## Setup flow (in the Laravel app folder)

```bash
npm install @kirschbaum-development/sst-laravel --save  # required: sst.config.ts imports it
npx sst-laravel skill:install            # install/update the skill (.ai/skills with Laravel Boost)
npx sst-laravel guide                    # same guide as the skill, from the installed package
npx sst-laravel doctor                   # readiness check
npx sst-laravel init                     # creates sst.config.ts (minimal)
npx sst-laravel deploy --stage dev       # deploy (vault-aware, use instead of sst deploy)
npx sst-laravel status --stage dev --url https://<url-from-deploy>  # verify tasks + /up
```

Install the package before any `npx sst-laravel` command. Until it is
installed, `npx` looks for a different, unscoped package with that name.

Never print secret values. Never put AWS keys in `.env` files. Never deploy to
`production` unless the user said so.

## Minimal config (web only, no domain, no database)

```ts
const app = new LaravelService("MyApp", {
  vpc,
  web: { size: "small", healthCheck: { path: "/up" } },
  config: { environment: { file: `.env.${$app.stage}` } },
});
return { url: app.url };
```

`new sst.aws.Vpc("MyVpc")` with no options is cheapest (~$0.50/mo). Without
NAT, containers run in public subnets with a public IP (~$3.65/mo each);
inbound traffic still only comes through the load balancer. Add `nat: "ec2"`
(~$13/mo) to keep containers private, e.g. for a fixed outbound IP. Avoid
`nat: "managed"` (~$73/mo) unless you need the scale.

Rough monthly cost of this setup in us-east-1: ~$46 (small container $18 +
its public IP $3.65, load balancer $16 + its 2 public IPs $7.30, VPC $0.50).

## Add what the user agreed to

Before any config, show the user a plan: what the app needs, questions
(database? background work?), what gets created and the monthly cost, how the
deploy works, and how to remove it (`npx sst remove --stage <stage>`).

```ts
const database = new sst.aws.Postgres("MyDatabase", { vpc }); // or sst.aws.Mysql, ~$14/mo
config: { deployment: { script: "infra/deploy.sh" } },  // runs on each start: put `php artisan migrate --force` in it
link: [database],                       // auto-injects DB_*/REDIS_*/AWS_* vars
link: [{ resource: db, envFrom: (db) => ({ CUSTOM: db.host }) }], // extra vars
web: { domain: "app.example.com" },     // custom domain (https)
web: { size: "medium", scaling: { min: 1, max: 3 } },  // small|medium|large; cpu/memory win
web: { scheduler: true, tasks: { queue: { command: "php artisan queue:work" } } }, // in the web container, no extra cost
workers: [{ horizon: true, scheduler: true }],         // queues / scheduler in a worker (~$22/mo)
reverb: { domain: "ws.example.com" },   // WebSockets (or `reverb: true`)
config: { environment: { secrets: env } },  // RemoteEnvVault instead of file
web: { advanced: { architecture: "arm64" } }, // SST escape hatch (experts only)
```

## Load balancer (web and reverb)

Secure by default, nothing to configure: TLS 1.2+ on the https listener, only
the listener ports open, invalid headers dropped, http redirected to https.

```ts
web: {
  loadBalancer: {
    ingressCidrs: ["173.245.48.0/20", "2400:cb00::/32"], // only these ranges (CDN/WAF) reach the load balancer
    accessLogs: true,                                    // access logs to a new S3 bucket, kept 90 days
    // accessLogs: { bucket, prefix: "web", retentionDays: 365 },
    // sslPolicy: "ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-Ext2-2021-06", // only to support older clients
  },
},
```

Only add these when the user asks. `ingressCidrs` blocks every other address,
so confirm the ranges first. `loadBalancer.accessLogs` is not `web.accessLogs`
(nginx logs in CloudWatch). `loadBalancer` only takes these three keys; any
other key fails the deploy. To define the load balancer itself (listeners,
ports), use `advanced.loadBalancer`. Guide: `load-balancer.md`.

## Before deploying

- `.env.<stage>` exists, `APP_KEY` set, `APP_DEBUG=false`, `LOG_CHANNEL=stderr`.
- Stage env file is git-ignored (`git check-ignore .env.dev`).
- `bootstrap/app.php` has `$middleware->trustProxies(at: "*")`.
- Docker is running (the image builds on this machine).
- No migrations at startup until a persistent database exists. Without a
  database, set `SESSION_DRIVER=cookie`, `CACHE_STORE=file`,
  `QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync` so pages still load.

## If /up is not healthy

1. `npx sst-laravel status --stage <stage> --url <url>` — tasks + health in one view.
2. `npx sst-laravel logs web --stage <stage>` — recent errors (stop it after reading).
3. Usual causes: missing `APP_KEY`, wrong env names, DB unreachable, wrong health
   path, AWS keys committed in the env file (use the IAM role instead).
